BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.2 percentage points in September, to 4.2%, its lowest level since October 2022.

Since January 2024, this metric has declined -3.4 percentage points.

The personal savings rate is now well below the 5-year pre-pandemic average of 6.2%.

This comes as personal income grew +4.1% YoY in September, its 2nd-lowest growth rate since April 2022.

At the same time, personal consumption expenditures rose +6.3% YoY, the 2nd-highest YoY growth since December 2024.

In other words, consumer spending continues to outpace income growth, putting further pressure on household savings and increasing household reliance on borrowing.

Elevated inflation and record prices are putting further pressure on consumer savings.

quoted.text:
A Stanford student got reported for academic misconduct last semester.

His research paper was so good his professor assumed he bought it.

The academic integrity hearing lasted 3 hours.

Here's what happened in that room.

The panel asked him to explain his methodology from scratch. He opened his laptop, pulled up http://Kimi.com, and started rebuilding the entire paper live in front of them.

First he fed it his raw notes and asked: "You are a research methodology expert. Here are my raw notes. Identify the 3 strongest arguments buried in this data, rank them by originality, and show me exactly where each one challenges or extends existing literature."

The professors went quiet.

Then he ran: "Now simulate a hostile peer reviewer with a PhD in this field. Generate every serious objection they would raise against my thesis. Then tell me which objections actually have merit and which ones I can dismantle."

One professor leaned forward and asked him to stop so she could write down the prompt.

He kept going. "Take my weakest argument and steelman it harder than I did. Show me what it would look like if it were airtight. Then tell me what I'd need to prove to get it there."

Then the one that ended the hearing. "You are my thesis advisor. I have 24 hours before submission. Read this draft and tell me the single change that would move this from a B+ to an A. Be brutal."

He walked them through how he'd used that last output to rewrite his conclusion three times until it held u

posts.name: Andy Constan
posts.text:
I have somewhat different view than most having cut my options teeth on a dispersion book during the tech bubble.  

The index vol short half of the short correlation trade was always a choice in terms of its sizing.  Back then IV/RV premium was pretty narrow unlike today so every unit of Vega sold in index was managed carefully.  Being short index vol was a coin flip sort of trade.   The sizing ranged from Vega neutral to single stock book (which collected theta) to theta neutral which was Vega long. 

The drop in implied correlation makes the trade less attractive.  But given the level of implied on index the notable risk isn't selling index vol to low its buying single name vol way way too high.  The root causes of that single name vol levels are numerous including speculative demand and the dispersion trader competing to buy elevated single name vol.  the seller is absent and gets a sweet risk premium when providing any liquidity. The risk the dispersionis at most risk to is a single name vol  collapse.  Perhaps a large equity drawdown would also be a negative single name vol event but that seems pretty unlikely.  So then it comes down to hedging index level and sizing.  

Is the CIO buying index puts to hedge the dispersion traders?  Jeez maybe but then the LP's are just long single name vol at extremely elevated levels.  

My picture is of course if macro drives index levels down index implied will get bid up but on the day so will single name vol.  

Frankly the responsible CIO would be finding ways to get short single name vol if they are really worried NOT buying index puts at 20+ vol

But mostly I don't see them hedging much at all

posts.name: GonzalesJ
posts.text:
Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way .

@robin_j_brooks is correct in this analysis. This is a regime shift, not a blip.

For most of 2026, oil up meant yields up. Inflation expectations fed straight into the long end. That link is now broken. The 20-day correlation between Brent and the 10Y has collapsed to its lowest since late 2024.

The reason is Europe. The French 10-year is at 4.96%, the highest since 2002. The spread over German Bunds has widened to 159bp, the widest since 2011. French debt-to-GDP is 117%, versus 90% at the last crisis peak.

Bessent confirmed this week that capital is leaving "concerning" jurisdictions and flowing into Treasuries as a safe haven. The US is catching a bid because the alternative is worse.

This is not a resolution of the fiscal problem. Net interest is still above $1 trillion. The term premium is being temporarily suppressed by a flight to quality, not by better US math.

If Europe stabilizes, the bid fades. If Europe cracks, the bid deepens.

The year is 1873. Your wife tires easily and reads too much. The doctor prescribes the rest cure: six weeks flat in bed, no books, no visitors, fed on milk, forbidden to sit up without his permission. The man who devised it is the most famous nerve specialist in America, and the women come out of it quieter, which is taken as the cure.

The year is 1915. The hospital has a new way of delivering your child. Morphine, then scopolamine, and the mother wakes two days later with a baby she cannot remember having. They call it twilight sleep. The women are strapped into padded cots so they do not hurt themselves while they scream, and the straps are the modern part. The babies arrive blue and slow to breathe.

The year is 1945. The truck comes down your street fogging DDT, and the children run behind it in the white cloud because the man on the back says it is harmless. At the beach it is sprayed over the bathers on their towels. It goes on the cattle, over the barn, and across the kitchen table.

The year is 1948. Your son has trouble with his ears. The doctor slides a rod tipped with radium up each nostril and holds it there for the best part of ten minutes, and you bring him back three more times. Hundreds of thousands of American children get the same treatment. The cancers arrive in their fifties.
